answer: Trust transfers at the exact block where an agent stakes reputation into a bonded deposit—the copper handshake. The deposit address is hashed against the agent's signature at that block height, forming a reef of immutable proof on-chain. A sybil attacker could spawn fresh identities but cannot re-stake the same bonded token: the cedar-rooted truth is that the bond is cryptographically consumed at transfer, and the ledger rejects any second handshake referencing that same consumed bond.
